ruling.recommended_action: Refund $3.46 to the rider's original payment method as the uninformed surge differential; no account flag (no repeat-deviation or no-show clause applies to this fare case).
ruling.reasoning:
The trip itself is not in dispute: actual distance 3.9 km equals the optimal 3.9 km, +0.0 km, so RD-1 leaves nothing to refund under RD-2 [F1][F3][RD-1][RD-2]. The whole $3.46 gap is the surge step from the quote at 1× to the 1.4× multiplier in effect at trip start, with the $1.25 booking fee not surged [F4][F6][F7][F8][FARE-0].

The decisive element is SURGE-1's notice, which requires the notice to state the new multiplier, the revised fare, and the free-cancellation right [F9][SURGE-1]. Code has settled that the surge rose between quote and trip start and that an in-app notice was delivered at 17:18:45, before the 17:20 start [F8][F9][SURGE-2]. Reading the notice's own words: "Fares are 1.4× higher right now" states the multiplier, and "You can cancel for free" states the cancellation right; but the third item reads "Your fare stays at the quoted $12.71" [F9]. Taken in context — a notice whose stated purpose is to announce a multiplier increase — that sentence tells the rider the price is unchanged, not what the revised fare will be; the rider was in fact billed $16.17 at 1.4× [F5][F7]. It is not a low or rough estimate of the revised fare but a contradiction of it, and an item contradicted within the notice itself is not stated [F9][SURGE-1]. The element therefore reads not_met.

The notice being defective, the case falls into SURGE-2's "surge rose, rider not notified" row, and the refund is the surge differential [F9][F8][SURGE-2]. The trace fixes the amount as (1.4 − 1) × surgeable subtotal $10.66 = $4.26, capped at the $3.46 by which the fare exceeds the quote, giving $3.46 [F8][F7][SURGE-3]. The driver's post-trip statement that the rider was told and chose to ride is a claim, not consent or accurate notice: it is not part of the timestamped chat and adds nothing where the platform's own notice text is defective [F13][F12][F9][SURGE-1]; the rider's two chat messages are only pickup logistics and neither acknowledges the surge [F10][F11][F12]. No route-deviation refund arises, and no repeat-deviation or no-show clause applies on these facts [F14][F15][RD-6][NS-2].

The safety screen found nothing: the complaint, the two chat messages and the driver's statement contain no threat, intimidation, harassment, abuse or dangerous-driving allegation [F10][F11][F13][SAFE-1]. The amount is $3.46, under $10, so the system rules finally under TH-1/TH-2 [F8][TH-1][TH-2].

Not relied on: the rider's silence about price in the two pickup-logistics messages [F10][F11][F12] does not by itself show she was misled; the finding rests on the notice text at F9 [SURGE-1].
